USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

A high-risk bezoar setting

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A hospitalized patient with impaired gastric emptying receives sucralfate through an enteral feeding regimen. New gastric retention raises concern for a medication-associated bezoar. Which feature most increases the relevance of this reported adverse event?

  1. Isolated seasonal rhinitis
  2. A healed skin abrasion
  3. Underlying delayed gastric emptying with enteral feeding
  4. Normal motility with no feeding tube
  5. A single remote H. pylori infection
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Underlying delayed gastric emptying with enteral feeding

Bezoars have been reported with sucralfate, especially where gastric emptying is impaired or enteral feeding is used.

Understanding the options

Underlying delayed gastric emptying with enteral feeding
Bezoars have been reported with sucralfate, especially where gastric emptying is impaired or enteral feeding is used.
Normal motility with no feeding tube
Normal transit lacks the key predisposing factor.
A single remote H. pylori infection
Remote infection alone does not predict this problem.
Isolated seasonal rhinitis
Rhinitis does not impair gastric transit.
A healed skin abrasion
A skin abrasion is unrelated.
